mission: Maintain candidate references for the Kamilah/Camilla Stevenson XRP/markets YouTube presence. Person identity is confirmed by first-person and branded-source evidence, but the canonical YouTube channel ID/handle relation remains probable rather than platform-verified. Do not treat candidate uploads as verified creator inventory.

identity_evidence: The first-person branded site identifies its owner as Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, also known as The Wealth Doctor.

In the 2026-06-11 iHeart XRP Podcast interview, the guest self-reports a YouTube display name rendered in the auto-generated transcript as doctor Camilla Stevenson and warns that fake pages exist; the transcript does not supply an exact channel URL.

The Linktree account @Dr.Kamilahstevenson links to a YouTube channel labelled Kamilah Stevenson and to the Kamilah Stevenson branded site; the retrieved branded site did not reciprocally link to the exact YouTube channel.
The Linktree YouTube link resolves to the candidate handle @drkamilahstevenson, but the YouTube page fetch was throttled and did not expose first-party About metadata or the canonical channel ID.
YouTube search results display Kamilah Stevenson as author for candidate videos; indexed author labels are not platform-side account ownership proof.

The first-party YouTube channel page at the canonical channel ID displays the channel title Kamilah Stevenson and handle @drkamilahstevenson on the same page, and links to go.prescribewealth.com/yt-bio. This verifies the platform channel ID/handle/display-name mapping, not civil identity.

Two first-party YouTube video search results display the author as Kamilah Stevenson and provide exact video IDs, publication dates and metadata. Their author bylines match the self-identifying channel display name; the individual video results do not expose a channel ID.

The channel-to-person association is strongly corroborated by the channel's branded external link, the first-party Kamilah Stevenson site and the iHeart interview self-identification, but no government identity record, platform verification badge or reciprocal first-party website link was captured.
caveats: YouTube first-party metadata now verifies the canonical channel ID, handle and self-identifying display name; it does not independently prove the operator's civil/legal identity.
The person-to-channel association is strong but not legal-identity verified. Preserve this distinction in all future attribution.
The iHeart transcript uses Camila/Camilla as an auto-generated spelling variant and warns about fake pages; do not merge unrelated same-name accounts.
The two video author bylines are first-party YouTube metadata, but the individual video results did not expose their channel IDs. Keep that limitation attached to each record.
The 21 earlier seed-video references remain candidate-only because their individual author/channel provenance was not upgraded by this channel-page capture.
YouTube subscriber/video counts and indexed view/like counts are dynamic crawl-time observations, not canonical current counts.

ingestion_policy.content_access: Public metadata and publicly available transcripts only; respect platform terms and access controls.
ingestion_policy.transcript_policy: Store transcript or authorized transcript reference where permitted; preserve timestamps and transcript hash; if unavailable, record unavailable scope rather than fabricate.
ingestion_policy.prediction_policy: Extract each explicit prediction with original publication cutoff, target, direction, horizon, probability/confidence if stated, assumptions, and later outcome. Do not infer an unstated probability.
ingestion_policy.evidence_policy: Creator statements are claims, not ground truth. Independently corroborate with primary filings, official statements, market data, on-chain data, regulatory records, and independent sources.
ingestion_policy.forecasting_policy: Never use a video published after the forecast cutoff as a feature for that forecast. Prevent look-ahead and survivorship leakage.
ingestion_policy.financial_safety: Research and shadow evaluation only; no trading instruction or live order execution.
ingestion_policy.identity_gate: YouTube first-party channel metadata verifies the channel ID/handle/display-name mapping. Two individual YouTube author-byline records are admitted to a partial channel-attribution inventory. The person-to-channel association is strong but not legal-identity verified; 21 earlier seed references remain candidate-only.

cross_corroboration_findings.claim: Confidential Transfers could improve institutional suitability by shielding MPT balances and transfer amounts while retaining cryptographic verification and optional auditor disclosure.
corroborated_details: The specification describes confidential transfers for Multi-Purpose Tokens using EC-ElGamal and zero-knowledge proofs.
The design preserves supply/accounting invariants and includes optional auditor encryption.
Feature availability and amendment activation must be checked separately from the existence of a final specification.
counterpoints: Technical capability does not prove banks have deployed it or that it increases demand for XRP as an asset.
The documented feature applies to MPT balances/transfers; it should not be generalized to every XRP payment or every XRPL transaction type.
The known-amendments page lists ConfidentialTransfer with default vote No in the latest stable release; activation status must be checked at each data cutoff.
cross_corroboration_findings.prediction_use: Do not encode as bullish price signal without independent evidence of activation, production use, measurable flows, and market response.

cross_corroboration_findings.claim: Sponsored Fees and Reserves may let an end user transact without personally holding XRP.
corroborated_details: The official documentation describes sponsors paying fees and reserve requirements for sponsees.
Sponsorship does not transfer XRP to the sponsee; the sponsor retains the XRP used to back reserves.
An official September 21, 2026 vulnerability report states the Sponsor amendment had not been activated on Mainnet at that report date and would wait for the fix in xrpld v3.4.0.
counterpoints: Do not describe the feature as live on Mainnet without a fresh official amendment-status check.
Lower onboarding friction could increase XRPL activity without proportionally increasing spot XRP demand.
The reserve sponsorship model itself has operational/security constraints and was subject to a disclosed Devnet vulnerability.
cross_corroboration_findings.prediction_use: Track amendment status, sponsor usage, new active accounts, fee/reserve sponsorship volumes, and market liquidity separately; no direct bullish inference.
